findings.text: Without a key a stored packet shows its payload length (44 for a cover packet, 31 / 329 / 3029 for texts of 2, 300 and 3000 characters in this simplified model). On the wire the size is always 4096 bytes. What leaks is the number inside the packet, to whoever can read the node's database or the relay. The way to close it is to put the length inside the encrypted part (a wire-format change for every client).

findings.text: The first 8 bytes of every stored 4096-byte packet are the payload length and the position of the payload, in the clear (NetworkObfuscation.kt, padPacket). The node stores the packet as received. So whoever can read a node's database can read each packet's encrypted length, which follows the message length, and a cover packet (44 bytes) is shorter than any real message. The size on the wire stays 4096 bytes. See 08 and PacketMetadataTest.kt.
